feedback.problem:
A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(0,-3).$ Find the polar coordinates of $P.$ Give the polar angle in radians and do not round the answer.

The polar coordinates of $P$ are $(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Since the point $P$ lies on the negative half of the $y$-axis, we have $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{2}.$ 

Therefore, the polar coordinates of $P$ are $(3,\frac{3\pi }{2}).$
